CheckpointManifestV1.description: The manifest.json written beside model.safetensors in every saved checkpoint. The trainer writes the fields marked 'Written by the trainer.' (BRD-02 R-02.20); the fields marked 'Written by whichever process writes the checkpoint' are written by miForge by default and by miLLM in the section 5.10 hot-update mode (BRD-01 R-01.12); kind and schema_version are constants. This file is the normative field list for both repos; neither BRD restates it. The directory it sits in is a standard Hugging Face model directory - model.safetensors, config.json and the tokenizer's own files at the root - and manifest.json is the only non-standard file in it and is purely additive: a consumer that ignores it still loads the model.

base_model.description: The root model this lineage descends from. For a model created from nothing (BRD-02 R-02.41) it is the architecture config the model came from, and parent is null. Written by whichever process writes the checkpoint — miForge by default, miLLM in the section 5.10 mode.
base_model.title: Base Model

created_at.description: RFC 3339 timestamp of the save. Written by whichever process writes the checkpoint — miForge by default, miLLM in the section 5.10 mode.
created_at.title: Created At

domain.description: Written by the trainer. What this run is biasing the model toward, or null when the run has no domain — a general from-scratch pretraining run (BRD-02 R-02.41) biases toward nothing. The field stays REQUIRED so that 'no domain' is asserted explicitly: null is a statement, an absent key is an omission.
domain.title: Domain

grader_hash.description: Written by the trainer. Hash of the grader configuration (BRD-02 R-02.10). Null when the run used no grader.
grader_hash.title: Grader Hash

merged_adapter.description: Written by the trainer. The adapter baked into these weights, or null when none was. A merged checkpoint has TWO ancestors — the base, carried by 'parent', and the adapter, carried here. Without this field two checkpoints at the same step with the same parent, one merged and one not, would be indistinguishable and lineage would be wrong. See BRD-02 R-02.45.
merged_adapter.title: Merged Adapter

name.description: The fully qualified name. Written by whichever process writes the checkpoint — miForge by default, miLLM in the section 5.10 mode. Format: '<base_model>:<run_id>:step-<step>', with step UNPADDED. This is the display and API form: what /v1/models lists (BRD-01 R-01.15) and what a completion reports as its resolved model.
name.title: Name

optimizer.description: Written by the trainer. Which optimizer produced this step, and whether its state was carried in or started fresh.

parent.description: Written by the trainer. The 'name' of the checkpoint this one descends from, or null for a checkpoint saved directly off the base model. This is the edge BRD-01 R-01.16 walks to build lineage.
parent.title: Parent

retention.description: Written by the trainer. The out-of-domain score at this step (BRD-02 R-02.17), carrying the floor the run stops at.
retention.title: Retention

run_id.description: Written by the trainer. Stable for the life of a run; a new run_id is a new branch (BRD-02 R-02.23).
run_id.title: Run Id

selector_hash.description: Written by the trainer. Hash of the selector configuration (BRD-02 R-02.10). Null when the run used no selector.
selector_hash.title: Selector Hash

signal_source.description: Written by the trainer. Which signal source produced the batches for this run (BRD-02 section 5.2).
signal_source.title: Signal Source

step.description: Written by the trainer. THE CANONICAL STEP NUMBER, as an integer. Every rendered form derives from this one value: the checkpoint directory is 'step-' plus this zero-padded to six digits (step-000500), and 'name' is 'step-' plus this unpadded (step-500). Padding in the path exists so directories sort lexicographically; it is a path convention, not part of the step's identity. Nothing may carry the step as a string of its own.
step.title: Step

test.description: Written by the trainer. The in-domain score at this step (BRD-02 R-02.16, R-02.18). Null when no test ran at this step.
test.title: Test

weights_sha256.description: Hash of model.safetensors. Written by whichever process writes the checkpoint — miForge by default, miLLM in the section 5.10 mode. miForge writes it under BRD-02 R-02.20 in the default path; miLLM under BRD-02 section 5.10. where it is only ever written from a clean parameter set (BRD-01 R-01.11). Verified on load (BRD-01 R-01.14).
weights_sha256.title: Weights Sha256

CheckpointManifestV1.title: CheckpointManifestV1

MergedAdapter.description: An adapter merged into a checkpoint's weights (BRD-02 R-02.45). The merge is in-place and irreversible — the adapter's contribution cannot be subtracted back out — which is why this record exists and why R-02.45 refuses a merge unless a checkpoint of the unmerged base survives.

manifest_sha256.description: Hash of the adapter's own manifest, so the exact adapter stays identifiable if its directory moves.
manifest_sha256.title: Manifest Sha256

name.description: The adapter's identity, as its own manifest names it.
name.title: Name

step.description: Which step of the adapter's run was merged.
step.title: Step

MergedAdapter.title: MergedAdapter

OptimizerIdentity.description: Which optimizer produced a step, and the provenance of its state.

config_hash.description: Hash of the optimizer hyperparameters (learning rate, warmup, betas, batch size, accumulation).
config_hash.title: Config Hash

state.description: 'restored' when optimizer state was loaded from trainer-state for the resumed step, 'fresh' when a new optimizer was started on loaded weights. BRD-02 R-02.22 requires this be recorded, because a fresh optimizer on a mid-run checkpoint produces a loss discontinuity that is otherwise unexplained.
state.title: State

OptimizerIdentity.title: OptimizerIdentity

ScoreRecord.description: A score against a named evaluation set at one step.

floor.description: The value the run stops below. Set for retention (BRD-02 R-02.25); normally null for test.
floor.title: Floor

set.description: Identifier of the evaluation set that produced this score.
set.title: Set

provider.description: Written by the trainer. Which inference provider produced this score (BRD-02 R-02.16, R-02.49): a score is only comparable against another taken the same way. Null when the provider was not recorded.
provider.title: Provider

ScoreRecord.title: ScoreRecord
